correctness.rationale: The shortest border is itself unbordered. If its length exceeded half the word length, two shifts by the corresponding period would give a shorter positive border; thus the two copies can be separated by a legal middle. For distinct endpoints exactly one of the two junctions forces a zero on a nonempty middle, giving M=1+zT=1/(1-z-tz²), and the empty middle is legal. For a singleton border 0 there is no extra constraint; for 1 the middle is nonempty with both ends 0 (the one-letter middle 0 serves both ends). These cases give (1) and induction gives uniqueness. The scalar recurrence, convolution and limit then follow by coefficient extraction and Binet. In the convolution the conjugate-root error summed with u_k≤phi^{k+1} is O(phi^{-n/2}), as is the omitted tail. Recomputing gives a K=10 lower bound about 0.13695 and the displayed density to double precision; the analytic enclosure in (4) controls further digits. Replay via RESULT.md (5)–(6) and the tail estimate; both checkers and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed. The claim is about linear no-11 words and contiguous borders only.

evidence: Let B(z,t) count the companion's unbordered 01-oriented words. Its exact decomposition says that every bordered oriented word is uniquely v m v with unbordered oriented v and middle empty or starting in 0; the other junction is unrestricted. With D=1-z-tz² those middles have series 1/D, and all 01-oriented legal words have series tz²/D. Consequently D B(z,t)+B(z²,t²)=tz² by direct additive marking. Reversal and the singletons give U(z,t)=(1+t)z+2B(z,t), exactly (1).

The scalar transform identifies p with the companion's p_*; with q=1/phi and scalar oriented T, both are 2q(q²-T(q²)). The companion also gives the leading parity constants with an O(phi^{-3n/4}) residual.
